questions.question: Define sustainable development and explain two key ideas in the definition.
questions.expected_answer: Brundtland Report (Our Common Future, 1987): development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. Needs: the essential needs of the poor must be met, so development continues and poverty reduction is a priority. Limits: the environment can only supply resources and absorb waste at certain rates, so we should live on natural interest not capital (forests, fish, groundwater). It includes fairness between generations and within the present generation; humanity uses about 1,7 Earths.

questions.question: Explain the three dimensions of sustainable development and describe a trade-off between them.
questions.expected_answer: Economic: jobs, incomes and an economy that lasts; social: meeting basic needs, reducing inequality, rights and participation; environmental: protecting ecosystems, water, soil, air and using resources sustainably. Trade-off example: a coal mine creates jobs and taxes (economic) but may displace families and harm health (social) and pollute water and add carbon (environmental). EIAs, community consultation and alternatives help balance them; win-wins include insulation, solar water heaters, wetland restoration. Section 24 of the Constitution protects the environment.

questions.question: Describe global efforts towards sustainable development and one South African example of sustainable development in practice.
questions.expected_answer: Rio Earth Summit 1992 (Agenda 21, precautionary principle); Johannesburg summit 2002; Millennium Development Goals 2000-2015; 17 SDGs adopted 2015 for 2030, applying to all countries; Paris Agreement 2015 (well below 2 degrees, pursuing 1,5). South Africa: Cape Town Day Zero 2018, limit of 50 litres per person per day (family of four 200 litres a day), use roughly halved and Day Zero avoided; or the just energy transition from coal (about 80 per cent of electricity) to solar and wind, JETP 2021 (8,5 billion dollars).
